researcher_notes: FULL-BATCH CONTINUATION RUN. These 5 files (AGV-Overview_DE_Flyer.pdf, AXL-iGo_DE_Brochure.pdf, Automation_DE_Brochure.pdf, Intralogistic-Systems_DE_Brochure.pdf, iGo_systems_DE_TD.pdf) were initially unidentified 'single-file brochure' candidates flagged in the prior continuation run's memory as possibly Linde-related due to the 'iGo' naming -- on inspection they are STILL GmbH (a DIFFERENT, already-in-DB company with 10 existing 'iGo'-branded products; STILL and Linde are both KION Group brands but are tracked as separate DB companies, correctly kept separate here). 'iGo_systems_DE_TD.pdf' (18pp) turned out to be the single richest source this run: a genuine multi-model VDI-2198 style technical-data document covering EXV iGo (1 model) and, critically, FM-X iGo as 5 distinct named sub-models (FM-X 12/14/17/20/25 iGo, payload 1100-2400kg) and MX-X iGo as a 3-way fork-mechanism/mast-height configuration matrix (2x Schwenkschubgabel + 1x Teleskoptisch). Automation_DE_Brochure.pdf and Intralogistic-Systems_DE_Brochure.pdf are company-wide marketing collateral with no new fillable per-model fields beyond what AGV-Overview_DE_Flyer.pdf and iGo_systems_DE_TD.pdf already provide -- skimmed, no new data found, still moved to Analysed since their content is now fully accounted for by the richer sibling documents.

products.notes: COMPLEX CONFIGURATION MATRIX, not split into separate products this run: this source document documents MX-X iGo as (at least) 3 configurations -- 2x 'mit Schwenkschubgabel' (pivoting push-fork, payload 1400kg, base Hub 6350mm or 12850mm depending on mast) and 1x 'mit Teleskoptisch' (telescoping table, payload 1100kg, base Hub 10000mm) -- differentiated by LOAD-HANDLING MECHANISM as well as payload/lift-height, unlike the FM-X family's clean single-axis payload variants. Per this agent's workflow guidance on multi-dimensional configuration matrices, this was NOT split into new products (the fork-mechanism axis has no direct AP0 field to cleanly separate on), and no conflicting value was overwritten -- the DB's existing lifting_height=14000 was cross-checked against this table's own p.14 extended mast-option matrix, which shows 'Maximale Lastaufnahme- und Absetzhöhe im Automatikmodus' (max automatic-mode load/drop height, as opposed to the raw mechanical Hub figure) capping at exactly 14000mm for the higher Triplex-mast configurations -- a clean, non-conflicting match once the right table column is identified, confirming the DB's existing figure is the AUTOMATIC-MODE operational cap, not the raw mechanical stroke. max_payload=1500 (DB) is close to but not identical to any of the 3 documented configs (1400/1400/1100) -- not flagged as a hard conflict given the configuration-matrix ambiguity, but worth a Tech Lead note that no exact match exists in this source.
